newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Indices in post-expiration calm.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Indices in post-expiration calm.

text.p: Activity in U.S. stock index options was slow in early dealings as the market drifted in typical post-expiration range-trading, traders said.

After handsome gains in stock prices last week, which some traders say were helped by Friday's April option expirations, the market was generally cautious about either jumping on the bandwagon or going against the upward bias, they said.
"I think after the past two weeks, everyone's taking a break," said Jack Callahan, an independent market-maker in the Chicago Board Options Exchange's S&P100 index options.

Although implied volatility levels had come down to the lower end of recent ranges, Callahan said he expected volatilities to pick up again as the week wore on as the market remained unstable on the whole.
He said the recent decline in volatilities merely reflected the stock market's gains last week and relatively narrow ranges in the past few days.
The CBOE volatility index was up 0.12 point at 20.60 at 1100 CDT/1600 GMT. The index reflects implied volatilities for near-month options in OEX, which was up 0.65 at points at 747.50.
Still, prospects lingered that the market's choppiness might not translate immediately into higher volatilities.

"The thing about this market is that it's not so weak that it's going to completely collapse but it's not strong enough to go anywhere on the upside," said Jerry Hegarty, an equity analyst with Thomson Financial Services.
He said that made it difficult for option buyers to make a decision, even though he saw a high likelihood that the market could retest April lows during the May options cycle.
Hegarty noted that one thing he would want to avoid was selling puts.

Along with prospects of lower stock prices, the recent volatility decline had slashed the risk-reward ratio for option sellers, even though volatilities were still high from a historical perspective. VIX, which had averaged in the high teens in 1996 and low teens in 1995, has been fluctuating in the lower 20s for most of this year.
"Put sellers here are taking on huge risks," Hegarty said.

Traders said concerns about earnings, particularly in the high-tech sector, were likely to be a source of volatility this week. International Business Machines Corp's results were due out on Wednesday.
IBM options were among the most active equity options on CBOE in morning trade, in both puts and calls.

Elsewhere, the energy sector was one of the strongest parts of the market as positive earnings figures for big oil companies began rolling out. The oil index .XOI on the American Stock Exchange was up 3.75 points at 389.00 at 1215 CDT/1715 GMT, with light option volume.
Early in the day, Exxon Corp announced record quarterly earnings of $0.87 per share, above forecasts for $0.83 and compared with $0.76 a year earlier.
